headline: SEPTEMBER WASDE PRINTS; BEANS GIVE BACK 24 CENTS
subheadline: Friday's WASDE report sent soybeans lower and corn sideways, while crude fell hard on the Saudi pipeline story reversing course.
lead: The September WASDE printed Thursday, and Friday the market said what it thought: soybeans at $12.99 gave back 24 cents, the sharpest single-session drop in weeks, while December corn at $5.32 actually added a nickel. The USDA printed something, the funds sold beans and held corn, and now the question is whether $12.99 is the new floor or the first step lower.
the_takeaway: Beans broke on the WASDE print; corn held. Watch which one was right.
teaser: The WASDE printed and beans sold off hard. Corn disagreed. Here's what to make of it.

one_number.unit: per-day supertanker rate, Middle East to China
one_number.context: Supertanker day-rates hit $800,000 on the Baltic Exchange's benchmark Middle East-to-China route as Gulf tensions mounted. That is not a freight number; it is an input-cost signal for every bushel of US grain competing against expensive seaborne crude for vessel space.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans up through $13.30. Beans closed Friday at $12.99, down 24 cents on the day. The call did not play out.
yesterdays_call.note: The WASDE was the miss. The September supply number was bearish enough to flush length, and the funds sold rather than held. Wrong direction, wrong read on the report.

sections.title: WASDE PRINTS; BEANS FOLD
sections.body:
- The September WASDE sent soybeans down 24 cents to **$12.99**, giving back most of this week's premium in a single session; USDA's report carried enough bearish signal on supply that the funds stepped out of their long position without hesitation.
- December corn at $5.32 bucked the grain selloff, adding 2.5 cents; the divergence says the funds read the corn number as supportive and the bean number as not.
- Chicago wheat eased a modest 2 cents to $7.11, caught in the general grain softness but not carrying the same WASDE weight.
sections.catalyst: September WASDE released Friday; soybeans sold off on supply data, corn diverged higher.
sections.bottom_line: Beans broke on the print; corn held. The two-way split is the week's defining trade.
sections.farmer_action: If you have unpriced new-crop beans, $12.99 is the line. A close below $12.85 next week says the WASDE break has legs; price on that signal, not ahead of it.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: the hold-through-WASDE call failed; 18 cents below the threshold.

sections.title: CRUDE FALLS ON SAUDI PIPELINE REVERSAL
sections.body:
- WTI closed Friday at $99.99, down 3.1%, as the market partially reversed the prior session's Saudi East-West pipeline strike premium; the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a July re-escalation that has built and unwound twice since April, is showing the same pattern again.
- The White House's reported consideration of the Defense Production Act to expand US refining capacity put a ceiling on the crude rally: the market heard that domestic supply response is on the table, and $100 became resistance, not a floor.
- **$99.99** is the exact level where the prior week's diesel-pricing urgency becomes a question again; fall fieldwork diesel needs still unpriced here are one more Middle East headline away from $104.
sections.catalyst: Drone strikes on Saudi East-West pipeline Thursday; White House DPA refinery discussion capped the rally Friday.
sections.bottom_line: Crude gave back the pipeline premium but the underlying story has not changed. Unpriced fall diesel is still a risk.

sections.title: CATTLE FIRMS; HOGS SLIP
sections.body:
- Live cattle at $219.62 added 0.8% on the week's close, holding inside a narrow range; feedlot margins remain deep in the red per the Drovers tracker, and the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, is still removing roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity.
- Feeder cattle at **$337.88** ran 1.6% higher, the better move in the complex Friday, with the screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder imports keeping supply tight ahead of the Aug 24 phased Douglas, AZ reopening that the market is still pricing.
- Lean hogs at $81.62 slipped 1.9%, the weak link; no specific catalyst in the hog bucket, looks like position-squaring into the weekend.
sections.catalyst: Cargill processing constraint ongoing; feeder supply tightness from screwworm border closure supporting feeders.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle acting like a supply-constrained market that has not resolved either the lockout or the border reopening.
sections.vs_yesterday: Feeders: ran higher as called; live cattle held the range exactly.

sections.title: MEAL AT 52-WEEK HIGH; OIL SLIPS
sections.body:
- Soybean meal at **$349.30** is sitting at the top of its 52-week range, a split from nearby beans that closed down hard; meal is doing the work alone, with crush demand holding even as the board sold off.
- Soybean oil at $70.66 gave back half a percent, which is consistent with the broader bean break; the ADM biofuels story rolling through the news wires says the structural demand case for soy oil remains intact, but Friday's price said the week's premium is done.
sections.catalyst: Bean selloff post-WASDE weighed on oil; meal held at 52-week high on separate crush demand.
sections.bottom_line: Meal at the 52-week top while beans break is a spread worth watching: crush margin compression is coming if beans don't follow meal lower.

outside_the_pit.title: White House Eyes Defense Production Act for US Refinery Expansion
outside_the_pit.body: With American refineries already running at 98% capacity and diesel above $6 per gallon, the White House discussed invoking the Defense Production Act to add domestic refining capacity. For producers, this is the policy signal that the diesel price story is now at the presidential-action level, not just a market aberration.

outside_the_pit.title: GAO Probe Sought Into USDA Trade War Relief Distribution
outside_the_pit.body: Lawmakers DeLauro and Bishop asked the GAO to investigate whether $12 billion in trade war relief payments under the FBA and specialty crop programs were distributed fairly. Producers who received payments or were denied them should watch this: a critical GAO finding could trigger repayment demands or new eligibility reviews.

the_more_you_know.title: The spread that tells you who won the WASDE: meal versus beans.
the_more_you_know.body: When beans break on a WASDE print but meal holds at a 52-week high, the market is saying demand for protein is real but the headline supply number was bearish enough to flush length. Friday's 24-cent bean drop against flat meal is that signal exactly. Watch the spread next week: if meal starts following beans lower, the WASDE break has follow-through.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn harvest pace matters. Above 10% harvested confirms the Belt is moving; below 5% adds weather-delay premium to December corn above $5.32.
Weekly Export Sales: soybeans under 300K MT after the WASDE break says the funds were right to sell; above 500K MT reopens the floor debate at $12.99.
Saudi East-West pipeline damage assessment: if export disruption is confirmed, WTI above $100 is the line that reopens the fall diesel pricing window immediately.
Douglas, AZ feeder cattle port reopening pace: any slowdown in the phased screwworm reopening that began Aug 24 would put a fresh bid under $337.88 feeders.

daily_quote.text: A crisis is an opportunity riding the dangerous wind.
